> Historical 0.5.0 document. In 0.6.0 the ordinary George UI exposes only direct exact arithmetic; the experimental modular API remains available. Current tests and measurements are in `DIRECT_REWRITE_CACHE.md` and `results/0.6/`.

# fomkyr 0.5.0: arithmetic, modular verification and signatures

## Release decision

**Use direct exact arithmetic with the new rational heap enabled.** It is the measured
performance improvement in this release. The modular backend is operational, but it
is experimental and opt-in because its full computation plus exact verification is
slower on the cases measured here. The signature implementation is an executable
Python research reference, not a production WASM F5 or cover-criterion algorithm.

The source is the supplied fomkyr 0.4.0 archive. No live George repository or deployed
site was modified. All four shared/unshared WASM32/WASM64 binaries are included.

## Matched end-to-end measurements

Each entry is the median of **three fresh processes**, four shared-memory WASM32
workers, Node v22.16.0, and the filesystem adapter for OPFS. The host reports five
logical CPUs (AMD EPYC 9V74). Both releases were built using the same Clang 17
`-O3 -flto` toolchain. Kernel budget: 128 MiB; reduction scratch: 32 MiB; hashBits: 16.
Detailed progress, Hilbert calculation and text export were disabled. Module/worker
startup and degree checkpoints are included. Modular times additionally include
all prime computations, canonicalization, CRT/reconstruction and exact certification.
Primes run sequentially; each uses the same four-worker scheduler.

| Case | Degree | 0.4.0 exact | 0.5.0 exact + rational heap | Speedup | 0.5.0 modular + exact verification |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Original-order FK6 | 9 | 1.260 s | 1.251 s | 1.01x | 3.894 s |
| Original-order FK6 | 10 | 11.720 s | 6.522 s | **1.80x** | 20.678 s |
| P6 coefficient stress | 12 | 0.702 s | 0.244 s | **2.88x** | 0.830 s |

FK6 degree-10 ranges were 11.334-11.998 s for 0.4.0 and 6.349-7.131 s for the new
exact mode. P6 is an algebraic coefficient-stress presentation, not an additional
physical theory. Degree 9 is effectively unchanged. These are not Firefox timings.
There is no extrapolation to degrees 15-20 and no claim to remove exponential growth.

Raw final trials and serialized bases: `results/0.5/benchmarks-final/`.
Earlier `benchmarks/`, `exploratory/` and `fk6-degree*-modular/` measurements are
explicitly exploratory and were not used in the table.

## Why the exact mode improved

In the degree-10 FK6 run only **44 out of 33,581** compact-integer heap attempts
fell back. Those few rows were expensive. An experimental 256-bit integer heap
handled only one of them: the main obstruction was not merely integer width, but
reduction by polynomials whose leading coefficient is not one.

The new C reducer retains reduced rational coefficients n/d in a bounded sparse
heap, cross-cancels common factors before products, and checks every arithmetic
operation. It clears denominators and makes the output primitive only at the end
of a successful reduction. **All 44 rows completed in the new tier.**

This is exact arithmetic, not floating point. Coefficients that do not fit the
compact representation, long-word cases, or insufficient working space return
to the existing arbitrary-precision reducer from the unchanged original polynomial.
The compact representation is therefore a fast-path limit, not a precision cap.
Per-worker working arenas remain budgeted. The option `rationalHeap:false` disables
this tier; finite-field calculations never enter it.

The timed outputs of old and new exact modes are **byte-identical** on all three
cases. Independent Fraction comparison also confirms the same leading words and
mutual reduction. The new FK6 degree-10 profile has 2,155 rules, 78,021 stored terms,
and 41,805,680 kernel-allocated bytes in the representative trial.

## What the modular implementation actually certifies

The new `arithmeticMode:'modular-verified'` factory path computes finite-field bases,
tail-reduces them, groups matching leading-word structures, combines coefficients
by exact BigInt CRT and rational reconstruction, and verifies the reconstructed
candidate over Q. Two matching primes are attempted by default; one is an available
experiment but is never sufficient by itself for acceptance.

The exact verifier is **reject-only**. A nonzero original relation or critical
composition rejects the candidate; it is not silently appended to make the test pass.
The candidate also needs the leading-word structure of an actual modular calculation
from the original input, not a supplied or guessed Hilbert sequence.

For homogeneous input, fix a finite bound D. Let I_Q be the input ideal, I_p its
modular specialization and J_Q the ideal generated by the candidate. In each degree
d <= D, the exact checks and modular witness establish

    dim(I_p,d) <= dim(I_Q,d) <= dim(J_Q,d) = dim(I_p,d).

The first inequality follows from rank specialization of the finite integer matrix
of degree-d context multiples of the input; the second from exact input membership;
the equality from the verified Gröbner property and equal leading words. Thus the
candidate generates the same ideal through D, without reconstructing all cofactors.
That matrix is a proof device and is not explicitly materialized.

This is specific to degree-bounded homogeneous computation, not an unrestricted
solution to modular Gröbner bases in free algebras. The literature's full signature
modular algorithm and cover verifier are not claimed here [1].

Prime checkpoints are field/content-keyed. Rational candidates live in quarantine
until exact verification passes. A failed candidate cannot publish a certified Q
checkpoint. Progress distinguishes prime-field milestones from certified rational
degrees and does not invent a global percentage or ETA. Exhausting reconstruction
resources either invokes the explicitly reported direct-exact fallback or returns
`MODULAR_UNCERTIFIED` when fallback is disabled. Null/unbounded-degree requests keep
the original direct exact path.

`certification.json` is audit metadata, not a standalone proof object. Replay still
requires the input, candidate, a modular witness calculation and exact checking.
Outputs are primitive-integer rows with `tailReduced:true`, `reduced:false`; dividing
each row by its leading coefficient gives the monic reduced Q representation.
The raw timed modular metadata predates this label-only correction; polynomials,
algorithm and timings are unchanged.

## Signature experiment: encouraging pruning, not a production speed claim

`research/signature_reference.py` uses actual bimodule signatures u*e_i*v, a fair
order, regular reductions, known-zero signature divisibility and singular criteria,
following the framework of [2]. Twelve bounded examples pass an independently
completed ordinary Fraction basis and critical-composition checks.

Turning zero-signature screening on within that same reference algorithm reduces
regular reductions from **1,516 to 692 for FK4 through degree 5**, and **1,046 to 464
for the homogenized Clifford example through degree 5**. FK6 through degree 3 saves
none (1,016 with either setting). These are ablations of the Python signature
algorithm, not comparisons against the production C kernel. Extra labelled rules
and scheduling/indexing costs can offset saved reductions.

There is no C/WASM signature scheduler, no full F5 trivial-syzygy implementation,
and no cover-criterion verifier in this release. A production port needs a bounded
bimodule divisibility index, signature-safe per-worker reductions and ordered commit
rules. This is a substantive algorithm change, not a checkbox on ordinary completion.

## Validation and boundaries

The full existing release suite passed after the new arithmetic was enabled. It
includes native and actual four-variant WASM tests, 37 algebra/field combinations
checked using serialized WASM outputs and an independent oracle, storage/capability
fallback tests, progress tests, installer fixtures and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.
The expanded suite adds:

- 10,000 independently checked compact rational arithmetic cases: 3,269 accepted
  exact operations and 6,731 correctly declined operations requiring fallback.
- 25 bounded rational-heap presentation cases, including nonmonic random inputs,
  independent ordinary completion and critical-composition checks.
- 15 modular correctness/failure tests, including bad lifts, an unlucky prime,
  rejection without publishing a Q checkpoint, memory/workspace exhaustion and
  all four WASM variants.
- 13 reconstructed-Q algebra cases checked against independent Fraction completion,
  critical compositions and Hilbert coefficients; these overlap the broader matrix.
- 12 signature-reference ablations; these also overlap the algebra matrix.

The physical-algebra matrix includes commuting polynomial/exterior algebras,
homogenized Weyl/oscillator, Clifford and sl2 examples, q-oscillator examples and
Fomin-Kirillov presentations. It tests the algebraic tools, not experimental physics
or a complete EFT operator-counting pipeline. Test counts are not additive numbers
of independent physical theories.

The large FK6 degree-9/10 and P6 degree-12 evidence is **differential against 0.4.0**,
not independent fresh completion at those bounds. The modular outputs are also
mutually reduced against the old exact output using Fraction arithmetic.
Actual Firefox/OPFS/GitHub Pages end-to-end execution and FK6 degrees 15-20 were
**not tested this turn**. Existing capability fallbacks were retained and tested in
Node. Browser process RSS is not bounded by the C allocator; active rows and basis
metadata must still fit memory. CRT has a separate logical JS workspace limit.

## Upgrade and reproduce

From the unpacked `fomkyr/` directory:

```bash
python3 tools/install.py /absolute/path/to/george --dry-run
python3 tools/install.py /absolute/path/to/george
```

Keep `Coefficient algorithm = Direct exact arithmetic` and `Exact rational heap`
enabled for ordinary use. George exposes the optional verified modular mode and
minimum/maximum prime settings. Deploy all updated JS and all four WASM files
together. ABI-3 serialized records are unchanged. Original pruning, worker, memory,
Hilbert, degree and progress controls remain available.

```bash
bash tools/build.sh
bash tools/verify_release.sh
bash tools/verify_experimental.sh
FOMKYR_BASELINE=/path/to/rebuilt/fomkyr-0.4.0 python3 tests/benchmark_modular.py
```

Benchmarks should run separately from test workloads. See
`docs/ARITHMETIC_AND_SIGNATURES.md` for algorithms, API and certification details,
and `results/0.5/release-validation.json` for hashes and precise evidence paths.

[1] C. Hofstadler and V. Levandovskyy, *Modular Algorithms For Computing Gröbner Bases
in Free Algebras* (2025). https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11606v1

[2] C. Hofstadler and T. Verron, *Signature Gröbner bases, bases of syzygies and
cofactor reconstruction in the free algebra*. https://arxiv.org/html/2107.14675v2
